edges.description: Defective Pol III lowers production of its small non-coding RNA transcripts (tRNAs, 5S rRNA, BC200).
Reduced Pol III transcript supply perturbs oligodendrocyte translation and myelin production.
POLR3A-related Pol III transcriptional deficiency underlies oligodontia, although the intermediate mechanism linking Pol III dysfunction to dental anomalies remains unresolved.
POLR3A-related Pol III transcriptional deficiency is associated with delayed tooth eruption, although the intermediate developmental mechanism remains unresolved.
POLR3A-related Pol III transcriptional deficiency underlies hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, although the intermediate mechanism linking Pol III dysfunction to endocrine involvement remains unresolved.
POLR3A-related Pol III transcriptional deficiency is associated with short stature with or without growth hormone deficiency, although the intermediate mechanism remains unresolved.
POLR3A-related Pol III transcriptional dysfunction is associated with progressive, often severe myopia, although the intermediate mechanism remains unresolved.
Oligodendrocyte and myelin dysfunction manifests as diffuse CNS hypomyelination.
Diffuse deficiency of CNS white-matter myelin directly manifests as CNS hypomyelination on brain MRI.
Hypomyelination and associated cerebellar white-matter and vermian involvement produce progressive cerebellar ataxia.
Corticospinal tract hypomyelination leads to pyramidal dysfunction and spasticity.
CNS hypomyelination in POLR3-related leukodystrophy is associated with extrapyramidal motor dysfunction manifesting as dystonia, although the specific intermediate pathway remains unresolved.
CNS hypomyelination and progressive cerebellar dysfunction in POLR3-related leukodystrophy produce intention tremor, although the specific intermediate pathway remains unresolved.
Cerebellar and corticobulbar white-matter involvement produces progressive dysarthria.
Progressive neurologic motor dysfunction in POLR3-related hypomyelinating leukodystrophy leads to worsening swallowing difficulties (dysphagia).
Progressive cerebral white-matter and callosal involvement leads to cognitive decline.
Childhood-onset CNS hypomyelination manifests clinically as gross motor delay and developmental regression.

nodes.description: Biallelic pathogenic variants in POLR3A (the largest, catalytic subunit of RNA polymerase III) reduce POLR3A protein abundance in fibroblasts and autopsied brain tissue and impair Pol III, the enzyme that transcribes many small non-coding RNAs including tRNAs and 5S rRNA. This is the proximal molecular lesion of HLD7.
